records.title: Plan cards and onboarding still advertise out-of-catalog features from two client-side price copies; Professional is still priced below Standard
records.evidenceAtHead: No change since the audit. `git log 92ccdba1..HEAD` on client/src/concept2cure/v2/fixtures/licensing.ts, fixtures/onboarding-data.ts, server/services/billing.ts and server/routes/billing.ts returns no commits. LicensingSurface.tsx has an empty diff. Onboarding.tsx only gained the 'Agency accounts' step (723395ed4). (1) Two client copies remain: fixtures/licensing.ts:68 LIC_DTC and :76-93 LIC_PRICING; fixtures/onboarding-data.ts:21 LIC_DTC and :41-57 LIC_PRICING. LIC_ARCHETYPES, LIC_BUNDLES, LIC_TIER_LEVEL, LIC_ROLES and licBundle are also duplicated across the two files. The server copy at billing.ts:193-321 is identical. (2) The feature strings are still '510(k) Module', 'CER Generation', 'Custom AI Models', 'On-Prem Option', 'SLA Guarantee' (pharma); '510(k) Workflow', 'eSTAR Builder', 'GSPR Mapping', 'EU MDR/IVDR Support' (medtech); 'Biostatistics Module' (academic). See billing.ts:206, 230, 251, 263, 275 and 303. (3) The price ladder is still inverted: Professional costs 399 against Standard 459 (pharma), 299 against 349 (medtech) and 119 against 149 (academic). The comment at billing.ts:211 says '$399 effective with 5+ users', but createCheckoutSession (billing.ts:383-391) applies BUNDLE_DISCOUNTS on top of the 39900 list price. So at every seat count Stripe charges less for Professional than for Standard. (4) Where it renders: LicensingSurface.tsx:97 reads LIC_PRICING and :499 maps t.features. Every user can reach it from the account menu (Shell.tsx:373 'View all plans') and from the lock panel CTA (navEntitlements.tsx:363-364 'View plans', ctaTarget 'licensing'). 'licensing' and 'onboarding' are LAUNCH_SHELL_SURFACES (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts:187-191). (5) New aggravating detail: Onboarding.tsx:358-385 provisionedFeatures() turns these marketing features into a list headed 'Modules provisioned for the <tier> tier' (:1094-1112). The server's provisionModulesForTier (billing.ts:943-976) actually grants modules by available_modules.metadata.tiers. So the wizard tells an org that '510(k) Module' and 'CER Generation' are provisioned when they are not. (6) GET /api/billing/pricing (routes/billing.ts:193-212) still returns a subset with no features, includedTokensMonthly or minCommitmentMonths. /dtc-pricing (:263-277) returns priceMonthly 0 for the custom-priced Enterprise tier (server baseMonthly 0). The client comment at Onboarding.tsx:261-265 admits the API is not a viable source. (7) There is no sync test or grep gate: `grep -rln 'LIC_PRICING|DTC_PRICING'` finds only the five source files.
records.remaining: All of it. (1) Client pricing constants are duplicated twice beside the server copy, and nothing checks that they stay in sync. (2) Feature lists include items outside the launch catalog, and 'Custom AI Models' conflicts with CLAUDE.md Rule 2. 'On-Prem Option' and 'SLA Guarantee' are unapproved contractual claims. (3) The ladder is inverted at list price and at checkout. (4) The onboarding 'Modules provisioned' list does not reflect what the server provisions. (5) The pricing APIs cannot serve the cards. Content decisions in (2) and (3) need the founder.
records.severityRationale: This is not a P0. The pilot is sales-led and its contract governs the commercial terms, so the in-app cards are not the offer of record. It is still P1 because every pilot user can open these screens from the account menu ('View all plans', 'Set up a workspace') and from every lock panel. The screens advertise modules the pilot did not buy and that the product does not ship, plus a Rule-2-conflicting 'Custom AI Models' and an 'SLA Guarantee'. The onboarding wizard calls these modules provisioned. The 'Choose' buttons start a real Stripe checkout on an inverted ladder. A GxP buyer's QA or procurement review would record this as a misrepresentation inside the validated system.
records.humanTestingNote: Symptom: account menu > 'View all plans' (or 'View plans' on any locked app) shows plan cards listing '510(k) Module', 'CER Generation', 'Custom AI Models', 'On-Prem Option' and 'SLA Guarantee', none of which are launch apps. In per-user mode, Professional costs less per user than Standard but claims 'Everything in Standard'. Account menu > 'Set up a workspace' > step 5 'Modules' lists those same features as 'Modules provisioned for the <tier> tier', while the rail and the Apps catalog show what is actually provisioned. Workaround: none needed to finish the journeys. Testers should log it as a known content defect awaiting a founder pricing decision, and should not click 'Choose <plan>' against a live Stripe key.
records.instructions:
1. Founder decision (blocking for content only): approve, per family (pharma, medtech, academic) and per tier, a feature list drawn only from the launch catalog: Projects, Vault, Authoring, Submission Center (eCTD v3.2.2 + FDA ESG), Submission Readiness, QMS controlled documents, the remote MCP connector, plus support/SSO/audit-pack items. Approve a monotonic price ladder. Decide with legal whether 'SLA Guarantee' and 'On-Prem Option' may appear at all. Record the decision in the commit message of the change below.
2. Server single source: in server/services/billing.ts PRICING (:193-321), replace every `features` array with the approved lists. Remove 'Custom AI Models' (CLAUDE.md Rule 2), '510(k) Module', '510(k) Workflow', 'CER Generation', 'Basic CER', 'Biostatistics Module', 'eSTAR Builder', 'EU MDR/IVDR Support', 'GSPR Mapping' and 'Predicate Intelligence' unless the founder puts them in the catalog. Set the Professional perUserMonthly values (:211, :256, :296) to the approved ladder and correct the ':211' comment.
3. Extract the per-seat amount logic in createCheckoutSession (billing.ts:383-391) into an exported pure function `computePerUserAmount(tierPricing, seats)` and call it from createCheckoutSession. Add server/services/__tests__/billing-pricing-catalog.test.ts that asserts: (a) for each family, computePerUserAmount for priced tiers does not decrease as tier level rises, for seats in {1,5,10,25,50}; (b) every feature string is in an allowlist built from shared/constants/launch-scope.ts LAUNCH_APPS labels plus the approved non-module items; (c) custom-priced tiers expose no numeric price. Run it before step 2 and show it failing (Professional below Standard; '510(k) Module' not allowed). Then show it passing.
4. Make the API servable: extend GET /api/billing/pricing (server/routes/billing.ts:193-212) to return, per tier, name, tier, perUserMonthly (dollars, null when custom), annualDiscountPct, includedTokensMonthly, maxProjects (numeric, -1 for unlimited), maxStorageGB, minCommitmentMonths and features. Add top-level `bundles` (BUNDLE_DISCOUNTS) and `tierLevels`. Accept a `family` query parameter alongside `industry`. Extend GET /api/billing/dtc-pricing (:263-277) to return baseMonthly null for custom-priced tiers (today priceMonthly is 0, which reads as Free) and numeric -1 for unlimited. Add a route test for both shapes.
5. LicensingSurface.tsx: remove the LIC_DTC, LIC_PRICING and licBundle imports (:16-23) and read `useLiveData('/api/billing/pricing?family=' + family)` and `useLiveData('/api/billing/dtc-pricing')`. Compute the bundle from the returned `bundles`. On a failed read, render dataConnect's ErrorState. Never fall back to a constant (fail closed). Rewrite the header comment (:8-14) and the footer note (:541-547) so neither claims a client mirror.
6. Onboarding.tsx: replace :322-327 with the same two reads, including loading and error states. Replace provisionedFeatures() (:358-385) and the step-4 block (:1094-1112) with one of two options. Option (a): a list of the modules the server would actually grant. Add GET /api/billing/tier-modules?tier= that runs the same available_modules query and tier comparison as provisionModulesForTier (billing.ts:943-976), sharing a pure helper so the two cannot drift. Option (b), if the founder prefers: relabel the step 'Plan includes' and show only the approved features. Rewrite the DATA HONESTY comment (:250-268).
7. Remove the duplication. Delete LIC_DTC, LIC_PRICING, LIC_BUNDLES, licBundle and their price interfaces from fixtures/licensing.ts (:15-40, :68-93, :108-113, :133-end) and fixtures/onboarding-data.ts. Keep one copy of the non-price constants (LIC_ARCHETYPES, LIC_TIER_LEVEL, LIC_ROLES) in fixtures/licensing.ts. Delete the duplicates from onboarding-data.ts, or the whole file if nothing else remains. Repoint the imports in surfaces/Onboarding.tsx, __tests__/onboardingActivation.test.ts, surfaces/licensing/TrialsPanel.tsx and surfaces/AdminSurfaces.tsx. No user-facing capability is removed: the plan cards still render at client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/LicensingSurface.tsx and surfaces/Onboarding.tsx, now from the API.
8. Add scripts/ci/check-client-pricing-constants.mjs (`npm run ci:client-pricing-constants`). It fails if any file under client/src exports LIC_PRICING or LIC_DTC, or assigns a numeric literal to perUserMonthly or baseMonthly. Add a `--self-test` that runs it on an inline fixture and shows it failing. Run it at HEAD first to show it failing. Wire it into the lint job of .github/workflows/ci.yml and into .husky/pre-push.
9. Update client/src/concept2cure/v2/__tests__/onboardingActivatesPlan.test.tsx to mock the two pricing endpoints. Add DOM tests showing that LicensingSurface and Onboarding render tier cards from the mocked API and render ErrorState (no cards) when the read returns 500.
10. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push there. Merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance:
1. billing-pricing-catalog.test.ts fails against the HEAD data (Professional below Standard; '510(k) Module' and 'Custom AI Models' outside the allowlist) and passes after the change.
2. `npm run ci:client-pricing-constants` exits non-zero on HEAD, its self-test shows the failure, and it exits 0 after step 7.
3. `grep -rn "LIC_PRICING\|LIC_DTC\|perUserMonthly: [0-9]" client/src` returns nothing.
4. DOM tests: both surfaces render tiers from the mocked /api/billing/pricing and /api/billing/dtc-pricing, and a 500 renders ErrorState with no price cards.
5. The onboarding step no longer says 'Modules provisioned' for anything the server does not grant. A test compares its list with the provisionModulesForTier helper for each tier, or the step is relabelled 'Plan includes' with approved features only.
6. /dtc-pricing returns null, not 0, for a custom-priced tier.
7. The founder's approval of the ladder and feature lists is recorded in the commit message.
records.dependencies: Founder decision on the price ladder and catalog-true feature lists; legal sign-off on 'SLA Guarantee' and 'On-Prem Option' wording. Steps 3-9 can be built in parallel against placeholder approved lists.

records.title: About 2,600 native nested CSS rules still ship unlowered (no build.cssTarget); five nested @keyframes are also dropped
records.evidenceAtHead: vite.config.ts has no commits since the audit (`git log 92ccdba1..HEAD -- vite.config.ts` returns nothing). At HEAD it still sets `build.target: 'es2022'` (:76) and has no `cssTarget`, `cssMinify: 'lightningcss'` or `css.lightningcss`. postcss.config.js runs only @tailwindcss/postcss and autoprefixer, and there is no browserslist. Vite 6.4.3 defaults `cssTarget` to `target` (node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/dep-Dm0c1Wj2.js:46102) and passes it to esbuild's CSS minify (:44347). @tailwindcss/postcss 4.2.2 quick-bails on any sheet without an import, reference, theme, variant, config, plugin, apply or tailwind at-rule. None of the affected sheets has one (grep count 0 for all ten). Commands run: (1) A postcss walk of every git-tracked client/src CSS file (scratchpad/reverify-ux06/count-nest.cjs) counts 2,607 nested rules in 10 sheets, up from 2,443 at the audit: misc-surfaces-v2 418, research-v2 386, authoring-v2 353, rbm-v2 348, ana-v2 237, device-v2 219, insights-v2 213, translation-v2 202, ectd-v2 183, protocol-dev-editing 48. (2) Vite's own esbuild 0.25.12 (node_modules/vite/node_modules/esbuild) run on authoring-v2.css with minify and target 'es2022' keeps 353 nested rules (output begins `.c2c-v2{.shell[data-editor=true]{...`). With target [chrome107, edge107, firefox104, safari16] it keeps 0. (3) A scan (scratchpad/reverify-ux06/kf.cjs) finds 5 @keyframes nested inside the `.c2c-v2{}` wrapper with no top-level definition anywhere: ana-v2.css acspin, authoring-v2.css dc-open, ectd-v2.css ecRise, research-v2.css pg-fade and pg-pop. esbuild leaves them nested even with browser targets. No CI gate, browser matrix or Playwright project for older browsers exists: playwright.config.ts has a single 'chromium' project, and no ci:* script checks built CSS for nesting. No built dist/ exists in the checkout, so built output was not observed directly; the esbuild run reproduces the exact Vite code path.
records.remaining: All of it. (1) Set build.cssTarget (or switch to lightningcss with targets) for an agreed browser matrix. (2) Add a CI gate on the built CSS. (3) Publish the supported-browser matrix. Also, outside the original finding: hoist the five @keyframes that are nested inside `.c2c-v2 {}`. Per the CSS Nesting spec, @keyframes is not a permitted nested at-rule, so those animations are likely dropped in every browser. This is inferred from the spec, not observed in a browser.
records.severityRationale: Downgraded from P1 for this pilot. The breakage only appears on Chrome/Edge before 112 (Apr 2023), Safari before 16.5 (May 2023) or Firefox before 117 (Aug 2023), all more than three years old in Oct 2026. A small or mid-size US biotech on managed evergreen browsers is unlikely to run them. The exposure is real for enterprise GA (pharma VDI and Windows Server 2012 images pinned to Edge 109), and a GxP customer's validation package will ask for a supported-browser statement. The fix is small. The founder should confirm the pilot customer's browser baseline at kickoff. If any pilot seat is below those versions, treat this as P1.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers on current Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox will see nothing. On an older managed browser (Chrome/Edge < 112, Safari < 16.5, Firefox < 117) the nested rules are discarded, and the editor (authoring-v2), Vault (misc-surfaces-v2), eCTD (ectd-v2) and research layouts collapse or lose styling. Workaround: test on a current evergreen browser and record the browser version in each bug report. Separately, in every browser, five animations (AnA 'acspin', editor 'dc-open', eCTD 'ecRise', research 'pg-fade' and 'pg-pop') probably do not run, because their @keyframes are nested in a style rule. A spinner or entrance animation may appear static. This is cosmetic only.
records.instructions:
1. Agree the supported-browser matrix with the founder. Proposed: Chrome/Edge >= 109, Firefox ESR >= 115, Safari >= 15.4. Confirm it covers the pilot customer's managed images.
2. In vite.config.ts, inside `build` (:70-76), add `cssTarget: ['chrome109', 'edge109', 'firefox115', 'safari15.4']`, matching step 1. Leave the JS `target: 'es2022'` unless the matrix needs lower. With esbuild, Vite's default minifier, this lowers nesting: verified with Vite's esbuild 0.25.12 on authoring-v2.css, 353 nested rules become 0. The lightningcss route (`build.cssMinify: 'lightningcss'` plus targets) is an acceptable alternative.
3. Hoist the five nested @keyframes out of their `.c2c-v2 { }` wrappers to top level, keeping their names: client/src/concept2cure/v2/styles/ana-v2.css `acspin`, authoring-v2.css `dc-open`, ectd-v2.css `ecRise`, research-v2.css `pg-fade` and `pg-pop`. esbuild does not hoist them even with browser targets.
4. Add scripts/ci/check-built-css-nesting.mjs. It parses every dist/public/assets/*.css with postcss and fails, printing file and selector, on any rule whose ancestor is a style rule, and on any @keyframes whose ancestor is a style rule. Like ci:component-class-coverage, it refuses a stale build or a missing dist (non-zero exit). Add a `--self-test` mode that feeds `.a{.b{color:red}}` and `.a{@keyframes k{to{opacity:1}}}` and asserts both fail. Add `ci:built-css-nesting` and `ci:built-css-nesting:selftest` to package.json.
5. Wire the gate into the `build` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml directly after the 'Build' step (:2284-2285), next to 'Component class coverage'. Run the self-test in the lint job.
6. Prove the gate fails first. Run `npm run build` before step 2 and run the gate: it must exit non-zero and report about 2,600 nested rules (source count at HEAD: 2,607 across 10 sheets). Apply steps 2-3, rebuild, and confirm it exits 0. Do this on a machine that may run a full build, not the shared 4-CPU audit box.
7. Publish the matrix in a supported-browsers section of the customer-facing validation and system-requirements material, and in docs/LAUNCH_DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md evidence if that file references client requirements. Optionally run a one-off manual or Playwright smoke with `executablePath` pointing at a Chromium 109 build over Vault, the Authoring editor and eCTD compile, and file screenshots.
8. Commit on concept2cure-v2 and push there. Merge, never rebase.
records.acceptance:
1. vite.config.ts sets build.cssTarget (or cssMinify 'lightningcss' with targets) to the published matrix.
2. `npm run ci:built-css-nesting` exits non-zero on a build made without the target and reports about 2,600 nested rules, and exits 0 after. Its self-test fails on both fixtures.
3. The ci.yml build job runs the gate after `npm run build`.
4. A source scan finds 0 @keyframes nested inside a style rule.
5. Vault, the Authoring editor and eCTD render the same layout on Chromium 109 (or Safari 16.0) as on current Chrome, with screenshots filed.
6. The supported-browser matrix is published.
records.dependencies: Browser matrix agreed with the founder and confirmed against the pilot customer's managed browsers. No code dependencies.
